   521→// countTranscriptItems counts lines (JSONL) or messages (JSON) in a transcript.
   522→// For Claude Code and JSONL-based agents, this counts lines.
   523→// For Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and JSON-based agents, this counts messages.
   524→// Returns 0 if the content is empty or malformed.
   525→func countTranscriptItems(agentType agent.AgentType, content string) int {
   526→	if content == "" {
   527→		return 0
   528→	}
   529→
   530→	// OpenCode uses export JSON format with {"info": {...}, "messages": [...]}
   531→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
   532→		session, err := opencode.ParseExportSession([]byte(content))
   533→		if err == nil && session != nil {
   534→			return len(session.Messages)
   535→		}
   536→		return 0
   537→	}
   538→
   539→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   540→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   541→		transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript([]byte(content))
   542→		if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
   543→			return len(transcript.Messages)
   544→		}
   545→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return 0
   546→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   547→			return 0
   548→		}
   549→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   550→	}
   551→
   552→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   553→	allLines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   554→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   555→	for len(allLines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(allLines[len(allLines)-1]) == "" {
   556→		allLines = allLines[:len(allLines)-1]
   557→	}
   558→	return len(allLines)
   559→}

   607→// calculateTokenUsage calculates token usage from raw transcript data.
   608→// startOffset is the line number (Claude Code) or message index (Gemini CLI)
   609→// where the current checkpoint began, allowing calculation for only the portion
   610→// of the transcript since the last checkpoint.
   611→func calculateTokenUsage(agentType agent.AgentType, data []byte, startOffset int) *agent.TokenUsage {
   612→	// No token usage information from Cursor yet
   613→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeCursor {
   614→		return nil
   615→	}
   616→
   617→	if len(data) == 0 {
   618→		return &agent.TokenUsage{}
   619→	}
   620→
   621→	// OpenCode uses JSONL with token info on assistant messages (different schema from Claude Code)
   622→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
   623→		return opencode.CalculateTokenUsageFromBytes(data, startOffset)
   624→	}
   625→
   626→	// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
   627→	if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
   628→		// Attempt to parse as Gemini JSON
   629→		transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript(data)
   630→		if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
   631→			return geminicli.CalculateTokenUsage(data, startOffset)
   632→		}
   633→		// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return empty usage
   634→		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
   635→			return &agent.TokenUsage{}
   636→		}
   637→		// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
   638→	}
   639→
   640→	// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
   641→	lines, err := transcript.ParseFromBytes(data)
   642→	if err != nil || len(lines) == 0 {
   643→		return &agent.TokenUsage{}
   644→	}
   645→	// Slice transcript lines to only include checkpoint portion
   646→	if startOffset > 0 && startOffset < len(lines) {
   647→		lines = lines[startOffset:]
   648→	}
   649→	return claudecode.CalculateTokenUsage(lines)
   650→}

   652→// extractUserPromptsFromLines extracts user prompts from JSONL transcript lines.
   653→// IDE-injected context tags (like <ide_opened_file>) are stripped from the results.
   654→func extractUserPromptsFromLines(lines []string) []string {
   655→	var prompts []string
   656→	for _, line := range lines {
   657→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   658→		if line == "" {
   659→			continue
   660→		}
   661→
   662→		var entry map[string]interface{}
   663→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &entry); err != nil {
   664→			continue
   665→		}
   666→
   667→		// Check for user message:
   668→		// - Claude Code uses "type": "human" or "type": "user"
   669→		// - Cursor uses "role": "user"
   670→		msgType, _ := entry["type"].(string) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion on interface{} from JSON
   671→		msgRole, _ := entry["role"].(string) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion on interface{} from JSON
   672→		isUser := msgType == "human" || msgType == "user" || msgRole == "user"
   673→		if !isUser {
   674→			continue
   675→		}
   676→
   677→		// Extract message content
   678→		message, ok := entry["message"].(map[string]interface{})
   679→		if !ok {
   680→			continue
   681→		}
   682→
   683→		// Handle string content
   684→		if content, ok := message["content"].(string); ok && content != "" {
   685→			cleaned := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(content)
   686→			if cleaned != "" {
   687→				prompts = append(prompts, cleaned)
   688→			}
   689→			continue
   690→		}
   691→
   692→		// Handle array content (e.g., multiple text blocks from VSCode)
   693→		if arr, ok := message["content"].([]interface{}); ok {
   694→			var texts []string
   695→			for _, item := range arr {
   696→				if m, ok := item.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
   697→					if m["type"] == "text" {
   698→						if text, ok := m["text"].(string); ok {
   699→							texts = append(texts, text)
   700→						}
   701→					}
   702→				}
   703→			}
   704→			if len(texts) > 0 {
   705→				cleaned := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(strings.Join(texts, "\n\n"))
   706→				if cleaned != "" {
   707→					prompts = append(prompts, cleaned)
   708→				}
   709→			}
   710→		}
   711→	}
   712→	return prompts
   713→}

   715→// generateContextFromPrompts generates context.md content from a list of prompts.
   716→func generateContextFromPrompts(prompts []string) []byte {
   717→	if len(prompts) == 0 {
   718→		return nil
   719→	}
   720→
   721→	var buf strings.Builder
   722→	buf.WriteString("# Session Context\n\n")
   723→	buf.WriteString("## User Prompts\n\n")
   724→
   725→	for i, prompt := range prompts {
   726→		// Truncate very long prompts for readability.
   727→		// Use rune-based truncation to avoid splitting multi-byte UTF-8 characters (e.g. CJK).
   728→		displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(prompt, 500, "...")
   729→		buf.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("### Prompt %d\n\n", i+1))
   730→		buf.WriteString(displayPrompt)
   731→		buf.WriteString("\n\n")
   732→	}
   733→
   734→	return []byte(buf.String())
   735→}

   737→// CondenseSessionByID force-condenses a session by its ID and cleans up.
   738→// This is used by "entire doctor" to salvage stuck sessions.
   739→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSessionByID(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
   740→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "condense-by-id")
   741→
   742→	// Load session state
   743→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
   744→	if err != nil {
   745→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to load session state: %w", err)
   746→	}
   747→	if state == nil {
   748→		return fmt.Errorf("session not found: %s", sessionID)
   749→	}
   750→
   751→	// Open repository
   752→	repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   753→	if err != nil {
   754→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
   755→	}
   756→
   757→	// Generate a checkpoint ID
   758→	checkpointID, err := id.Generate()
   759→	if err != nil {
   760→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   761→	}
   762→
   763→	// Check if shadow branch exists (required for condensation)
   764→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   765→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   766→	_, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   767→	hasShadowBranch := refErr == nil
   768→
   769→	if !hasShadowBranch {
   770→		// No shadow branch means no checkpoint data to condense.
   771→		// Just clean up the state file.
   772→		logging.Info(logCtx, "no shadow branch for session, clearing state only",
   773→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   774→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   775→		)
   776→		if err := s.clearSessionState(ctx, sessionID); err != nil {
   777→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to clear session state: %w", err)
   778→		}
   779→		return nil
   780→	}
   781→
   782→	// Condense the session
   783→	result, err := s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
   784→	if err != nil {
   785→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to condense session: %w", err)
   786→	}
   787→
   788→	logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed by ID",
   789→		slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   790→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   791→		slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   792→	)
   793→
   794→	// Update session state: reset step count and transition to idle
   795→	state.StepCount = 0
   796→	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   797→	state.Phase = session.PhaseIdle
   798→	state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   799→	state.AttributionBaseCommit = state.BaseCommit
   800→	state.PromptAttributions = nil
   801→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil
   802→
   803→	if err := s.saveSessionState(ctx, state); err != nil {
   804→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session state: %w", err)
   805→	}
   806→
   807→	// Clean up shadow branch if no other sessions need it
   808→	if err := s.cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused(ctx, repo, shadowBranchName, sessionID); err != nil {

   810→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   811→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),

   813→		// Non-fatal: condensation succeeded, shadow branch cleanup is best-effort
   814→	}

   816→	return nil
   817→}
   818→
   819→// cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused deletes a shadow branch if no other active sessions reference it.
   820→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused(ctx context.Context, _ *git.Repository, shadowBranchName, excludeSessionID string) error {
   821→	// List all session states to check if any other session uses this shadow branch
   822→	allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates(ctx)
   823→	if err != nil {
   824→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to list session states: %w", err)
   825→	}
   826→
   827→	for _, state := range allStates {
   828→		if state.SessionID == excludeSessionID {
   829→			continue
   830→		}
   831→		otherShadow := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   832→		if otherShadow == shadowBranchName && state.StepCount > 0 {
   833→			// Another session still needs this shadow branch
   834→			return nil
   835→		}
   836→	}
   837→
   838→	// No other sessions need it, delete the shadow branch via CLI
   839→	// (go-git v5's RemoveReference doesn't persist with packed refs/worktrees)
   840→	if err := DeleteBranchCLI(ctx, shadowBranchName); err != nil {
   841→		// Branch already gone is not an error
   842→		if errors.Is(err, ErrBranchNotFound) {
   843→			return nil
   844→		}
   845→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove shadow branch: %w", err)
   846→	}
   847→	return nil
   848→}

   383→}

   387→// addGeminiHook adds a hook entry to matchers.
   388→// Unlike Claude Code, Gemini hooks require a "name" field.
   389→func addGeminiHook(matchers []GeminiHookMatcher, matcherName, hookName, command string) []GeminiHookMatcher {
   390→	entry := GeminiHookEntry{
   391→		Name:    hookName,
   392→		Type:    "command",
   393→		Command: command,
   394→	}
   395→
   396→	// Find or create matcher
   397→	for i, matcher := range matchers {
   398→		if matcher.Matcher == matcherName {
   399→			matchers[i].Hooks = append(matchers[i].Hooks, entry)
   400→			return matchers
   401→		}
   402→	}
   403→
   404→	// Create new matcher
   405→	newMatcher := GeminiHookMatcher{
   406→		Hooks: []GeminiHookEntry{entry},
   407→	}
   408→	if matcherName != "" {
   409→		newMatcher.Matcher = matcherName
   410→	}
   411→	return append(matchers, newMatcher)
   412→}

   414→// isEntireHook checks if a command is an Entire hook
   415→func isEntireHook(command string) bool {
   416→	for _, prefix := range entireHookPrefixes {
   417→		if strings.HasPrefix(command, prefix) {
   418→			return true
   419→		}
   420→	}
   421→	return false
   422→}

   425→func hasEntireHook(matchers []GeminiHookMatcher) bool {
   426→	for _, matcher := range matchers {
   427→		for _, hook := range matcher.Hooks {
   428→			if isEntireHook(hook.Command) {
   429→				return true
   430→			}
   431→		}
   432→	}
   433→	return false
   434→}

   436→// getFirstEntireHookCommand returns the command of the first Entire hook found, or empty string
   437→func getFirstEntireHookCommand(matchers []GeminiHookMatcher) string {
   438→	for _, matcher := range matchers {
   439→		for _, hook := range matcher.Hooks {
   440→			if isEntireHook(hook.Command) {
   441→				return hook.Command
   442→			}
   443→		}
   444→	}
   445→	return ""
   446→}
   447→
   448→// removeEntireHooks removes all Entire hooks from a list of matchers
   449→func removeEntireHooks(matchers []GeminiHookMatcher) []GeminiHookMatcher {
   450→	result := make([]GeminiHookMatcher, 0, len(matchers))
   451→	for _, matcher := range matchers {
   452→		filteredHooks := make([]GeminiHookEntry, 0, len(matcher.Hooks))

   457→		}

   459→		if len(filteredHooks) > 0 {
   460→			matcher.Hooks = filteredHooks
   461→			result = append(result, matcher)
   462→		}
   463→	}

   257→// The level parameter specifies the log level (use slog.LevelDebug, slog.LevelInfo, etc).

   295→		allAttrs = append(allAttrs, a)
   296→	}

   298→	// Add caller-provided attributes

   322→	}
   323→	if v := ctx.Value(parentSessionIDKey); v != nil {

   328→	if v := ctx.Value(toolCallIDKey); v != nil {

   333→	if v := ctx.Value(componentKey); v != nil {
   334→		if s, ok := v.(string); ok && s != "" {

   338→	if v := ctx.Value(agentKey); v != nil {

    51→// WriteTemporary writes a temporary checkpoint to a shadow branch.
    52→// Shadow branches are named entire/<base-commit-short-hash>.
    53→// Returns the result containing commit hash and whether it was skipped.
    54→// If the new tree hash matches the last checkpoint's tree hash, the checkpoint
    55→// is skipped to avoid duplicate commits (deduplication).
    56→func (s *GitStore) WriteTemporary(ctx context.Context, opts WriteTemporaryOptions) (WriteTemporaryResult, error) {
    57→	// Validate base commit - required for shadow branch naming
    58→	if opts.BaseCommit == "" {
    59→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, errors.New("BaseCommit is required for temporary checkpoint")
    60→	}
    61→
    62→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
    63→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
    64→		return WriteTemporaryResult{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid temporary checkpoint options: %w", err)
    65→	}

    74→	}
    75→
    76→	// Get the last checkpoint's tree hash for deduplication
    77→	var lastTreeHash plumbing.Hash
    78→	if parentHash != plumbing.ZeroHash {
    79→		if lastCommit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(parentHash); err == nil {
    80→			lastTreeHash = lastCommit.TreeHash
    81→		}

    83→
    84→	// Collect all files to include
    85→	var allFiles []string
    86→	var allDeletedFiles []string
    87→	if opts.IsFirstCheckpoint {

    89→		// using `git status --porcelain -z` which respects both repo and global .gitignore.
    90→		// This is much faster than filesystem walk. The base tree from HEAD already contains

    92→		result, err := collectChangedFiles(ctx, s.repo)

   273→	if err != nil {

   275→	}
   276→
   277→	// Update shadow branch reference
   278→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   279→	ref := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitHash)
   280→	if err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(ref); err != nil {
   281→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to update shadow branch reference: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	return commitHash, nil
   285→}

   287→// addTaskMetadataToTree adds task checkpoint metadata to a git tree.
   288→// When IsIncremental is true, only adds the incremental checkpoint file.
   289→func (s *GitStore) addTaskMetadataToTree(ctx context.Context, baseTreeHash plumbing.Hash, opts WriteTemporaryTaskOptions) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   290→	// Get base tree and flatten it
   291→	baseTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(baseTreeHash)
   292→	if err != nil {
   293→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
   294→	}
   295→
   296→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   297→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, baseTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   298→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten tree: %w", err)
   299→	}
   300→
   301→	// Compute metadata paths
   302→	sessionMetadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + opts.SessionID
   303→	taskMetadataDir := sessionMetadataDir + "/tasks/" + opts.ToolUseID
   304→
   305→	if opts.IsIncremental {
   306→		// Incremental checkpoint: only add the checkpoint file
   307→		// Use proper JSON marshaling to handle nil/empty IncrementalData correctly
   308→		var incData []byte
   309→		if opts.IncrementalData != nil {
   310→			incData, err = redact.JSONLBytes(opts.IncrementalData)
   311→			if err != nil {
   312→				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to redact incremental checkpoint: %w", err)
   313→			}
   314→		}
   315→		incrementalCheckpoint := struct {
   316→			Type      string          `json:"type"`
   317→			ToolUseID string          `json:"tool_use_id"`
   318→			Timestamp time.Time       `json:"timestamp"`
   319→			Data      json.RawMessage `json:"data"`
   320→		}{
   321→			Type:      opts.IncrementalType,
   322→			ToolUseID: opts.ToolUseID,
   323→			Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
   324→			Data:      incData,
   325→		}
   326→		cpData, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(incrementalCheckpoint, "", "  ")
   327→		if err != nil {
   328→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal incremental checkpoint: %w", err)
   329→		}
   330→
   331→		cpBlobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, cpData)
   332→		if err != nil {
   333→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create incremental checkpoint blob: %w", err)
   334→		}
   335→		cpFilename := fmt.Sprintf("%03d-%s.json", opts.IncrementalSequence, opts.ToolUseID)
   336→		cpPath := taskMetadataDir + "/checkpoints/" + cpFilename
   337→		entries[cpPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   338→			Name: cpPath,
   339→			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   340→			Hash: cpBlobHash,
   341→		}
   342→	} else {
   343→		// Final checkpoint: add transcripts and checkpoint.json
   344→
   345→		// Add session transcript (with chunking support for large transcripts)
   346→		if opts.TranscriptPath != "" {
   347→			if transcriptContent, readErr := os.ReadFile(opts.TranscriptPath); readErr == nil {
   348→				// Detect agent type from content for proper chunking
   349→				agentType := agent.DetectAgentTypeFromContent(transcriptContent)
   350→
   351→				// Chunk if necessary
   352→				chunks, chunkErr := agent.ChunkTranscript(ctx, transcriptContent, agentType)
   353→				if chunkErr != nil {
   354→					logging.Warn(ctx, "failed to chunk transcript, checkpoint will be saved without transcript",
   355→						slog.String("error", chunkErr.Error()),
   356→						slog.String("session_id", opts.SessionID),
   357→					)
   358→				} else {
   359→					for i, chunk := range chunks {
   360→						chunkPath := sessionMetadataDir + "/" + agent.ChunkFileName(paths.TranscriptFileName, i)
   361→						blobHash, blobErr := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, chunk)
   362→						if blobErr != nil {
   363→							logging.Warn(ctx, "failed to create blob for transcript chunk",
   364→								slog.String("error", blobErr.Error()),
   365→								slog.String("session_id", opts.SessionID),
   366→								slog.Int("chunk_index", i),
   367→							)
   368→							continue
   369→						}
   370→						entries[chunkPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   371→							Name: chunkPath,
   372→							Mode: filemode.Regular,
   373→							Hash: blobHash,
   374→						}
   375→					}
   376→				}
   377→			}
   378→		}
   379→
   380→		// Add subagent transcript if available
   381→		if opts.SubagentTranscriptPath != "" && opts.AgentID != "" {
   382→			if agentContent, readErr := os.ReadFile(opts.SubagentTranscriptPath); readErr == nil {
   383→				redacted, jsonlErr := redact.JSONLBytes(agentContent)
   384→				if jsonlErr != nil {
   385→					logging.Warn(ctx, "subagent transcript is not valid JSONL, falling back to plain redaction",
   386→						slog.String("path", opts.SubagentTranscriptPath),
   387→						slog.String("error", jsonlErr.Error()),
   388→					)
   389→					redacted = redact.Bytes(agentContent)
   390→				}
   391→				agentContent = redacted
   392→				if blobHash, blobErr := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, agentContent); blobErr == nil {
   393→					agentPath := taskMetadataDir + "/agent-" + opts.AgentID + ".jsonl"
   394→					entries[agentPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   395→						Name: agentPath,
   396→						Mode: filemode.Regular,
   397→						Hash: blobHash,
   398→					}
   399→				}
   400→			}
   401→		}
   402→
   403→		// Add checkpoint.json
   404→		checkpointJSON := fmt.Sprintf(`{
   405→  "session_id": %q,
   406→  "tool_use_id": %q,
   407→  "checkpoint_uuid": %q,
   408→  "agent_id": %q
   409→}`, opts.SessionID, opts.ToolUseID, opts.CheckpointUUID, opts.AgentID)
   410→
   411→		blobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(checkpointJSON))
   412→		if err != nil {
   413→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to create checkpoint blob: %w", err)
   414→		}
   415→		checkpointPath := taskMetadataDir + "/checkpoint.json"
   416→		entries[checkpointPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   417→			Name: checkpointPath,
   418→			Mode: filemode.Regular,
   419→			Hash: blobHash,
   420→		}
   421→	}
   422→
   423→	// Build new tree from entries
   424→	return BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   425→}

   443→// listCheckpointsForBranch lists checkpoint commits for a specific shadow branch name.
   444→// This is an internal helper used by ListTemporaryCheckpoints, ListCheckpointsForBranch, and ListAllTemporaryCheckpoints.
   445→func (s *GitStore) listCheckpointsForBranch(ctx context.Context, shadowBranchName, sessionID string, limit int) ([]TemporaryCheckpointInfo, error) {
   446→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   447→
   448→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   449→
   450→	ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   451→	if err != nil {
   452→		return nil, nil //nolint:nilerr // No shadow branch is expected case
   453→	}
   454→
   455→	iter, err := s.repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: ref.Hash()})
   456→	if err != nil {
   457→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit log: %w", err)
   458→	}
   459→
   460→	var results []TemporaryCheckpointInfo
   461→	count := 0
   462→
   463→	err = iter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
   464→		if count >= limit*5 { // Scan more to allow for session filtering
   465→			return errStop
   466→		}
   467→		count++
   468→
   469→		// Verify commit belongs to target session via Entire-Session trailer
   470→		commitSessionID, hasTrailer := trailers.ParseSession(c.Message)
   471→		if !hasTrailer {
   472→			return nil // Skip commits without session trailer
   473→		}
   474→		if sessionID != "" && commitSessionID != sessionID {
   475→			return nil // Skip commits from other sessions
   476→		}
   477→
   478→		// Get first line of message
   479→		message := c.Message
   480→		if idx := strings.Index(message, "\n"); idx > 0 {
   481→			message = message[:idx]
   482→		}
   483→
   484→		info := TemporaryCheckpointInfo{
   485→			CommitHash: c.Hash,
   486→			Message:    message,
   487→			SessionID:  commitSessionID,
   488→			Timestamp:  c.Author.When,
   489→		}
   490→
   491→		// Check for task checkpoint first
   492→		taskMetadataDir, foundTask := trailers.ParseTaskMetadata(c.Message)
   493→		if foundTask {
   494→			info.IsTaskCheckpoint = true
   495→			info.MetadataDir = taskMetadataDir
   496→			info.ToolUseID = extractToolUseIDFromPath(taskMetadataDir)
   497→		} else {
   498→			metadataDir, found := trailers.ParseMetadata(c.Message)
   499→			if found {
   500→				info.MetadataDir = metadataDir
   501→			}
   502→		}
   503→
   504→		results = append(results, info)
   505→
   506→		if len(results) >= limit {
   507→			return errStop
   508→		}
   509→		return nil
   510→	})
   511→
   512→	if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errStop) {
   513→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("error iterating commits: %w", err)
   514→	}
   515→
   516→	return results, nil
   517→}

   563→// GetTranscriptFromCommit retrieves the transcript from a specific commit's tree.
   564→// This is used for shadow branch checkpoints where the transcript is stored in the commit tree
   565→// rather than on the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
   566→// commitHash is the commit to read from, metadataDir is the path within the tree.
   567→// agentType is used for reassembling chunked transcripts in the correct format.
   568→// Handles both chunked and non-chunked transcripts.
   569→func (s *GitStore) GetTranscriptFromCommit(ctx context.Context, commitHash plumbing.Hash, metadataDir string, agentType agent.AgentType) ([]byte, error) {
   570→	commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(commitHash)
   571→	if err != nil {
   572→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
   573→	}
   574→
   575→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   576→	if err != nil {
   577→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   578→	}
   579→
   580→	// Try to get the metadata subtree for chunk detection
   581→	subTree, subTreeErr := tree.Tree(metadataDir)
   582→	if subTreeErr == nil {
   583→		// Use the helper function that handles chunking
   584→		transcript, err := readTranscriptFromTree(ctx, subTree, agentType)
   585→		if err == nil && transcript != nil {
   586→			return transcript, nil
   587→		}
   588→	}
   589→
   590→	// Fall back to direct file access (for backwards compatibility)
   591→	transcriptPath := metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName
   592→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(transcriptPath); fileErr == nil {
   593→		content, contentErr := file.Contents()
   594→		if contentErr == nil {
   595→			return []byte(content), nil
   596→		}
   597→	}
   598→
   599→	transcriptPath = metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy
   600→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(transcriptPath); fileErr == nil {
   601→		content, contentErr := file.Contents()
   602→		if contentErr == nil {
   603→			return []byte(content), nil
   604→		}
   605→	}
   606→
   607→	return nil, ErrNoTranscript
   608→}

   619→// DeleteShadowBranch deletes the shadow branch for the given base commit and worktree.
   620→// worktreeID should be empty for main worktree or the internal git worktree name for linked worktrees.
   621→// Uses git CLI instead of go-git's RemoveReference because go-git v5 doesn't properly
   622→// persist deletions with packed refs or worktrees.
   623→func (s *GitStore) DeleteShadowBranch(ctx context.Context, baseCommit, worktreeID string) error {
   624→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID)
   625→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "branch", "-D", "--", shadowBranchName) //nolint:gosec // shadowBranchName is constructed from commit hash, not user input
   626→	if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   627→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete shadow branch %s: %s: %w", shadowBranchName, strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), err)
   628→	}
   629→	return nil
   630→}

   632→// ShadowBranchNameForCommit returns the shadow branch name for a base commit hash
   633→// and worktree identifier. The worktree ID should be empty for the main worktree
   634→// or the internal git worktree name for linked worktrees.
   635→// Format: entire/<commit[:7]>-<hash(worktreeID)[:6]>
   636→func ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit, worktreeID string) string {
   637→	commitPart := baseCommit
   638→	if len(baseCommit) >= ShadowBranchHashLength {
   639→		commitPart = baseCommit[:ShadowBranchHashLength]
   640→	}
   641→	worktreeHash := HashWorktreeID(worktreeID)
   642→	return ShadowBranchPrefix + commitPart + "-" + worktreeHash
   643→}
   644→
   645→// ParseShadowBranchName extracts the commit prefix and worktree hash from a shadow branch name.
   646→// Input format: "entire/<commit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>"
   647→// Returns (commitPrefix, worktreeHash, ok). Returns ("", "", false) if not a valid shadow branch.
   648→func ParseShadowBranchName(branchName string) (commitPrefix, worktreeHash string, ok bool) {
   649→	if !strings.HasPrefix(branchName, ShadowBranchPrefix) {
   650→		return "", "", false
   651→	}
   652→	suffix := strings.TrimPrefix(branchName, ShadowBranchPrefix)
   653→
   654→	// Find the last dash - everything before is commit prefix, after is worktree hash
   655→	lastDash := strings.LastIndex(suffix, "-")
   656→	if lastDash == -1 || lastDash == 0 || lastDash == len(suffix)-1 {
   657→		// No dash, or dash at start/end - invalid format
   658→		// Could be old format "entire/<commit[:7]>" without worktree hash
   659→		return suffix, "", true // Return as commit prefix with empty worktree hash
   660→	}
   661→
   662→	return suffix[:lastDash], suffix[lastDash+1:], true
   663→}

   766→// createCommit creates a commit object.
   767→func (s *GitStore) createCommit(treeHash, parentHash plumbing.Hash, message, authorName, authorEmail string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   768→	now := time.Now()
   769→	sig := object.Signature{
   770→		Name:  authorName,
   771→		Email: authorEmail,
   772→		When:  now,
   773→	}
   774→
   775→	commit := &object.Commit{
   776→		TreeHash:  treeHash,
   777→		Author:    sig,
   778→		Committer: sig,
   779→		Message:   message,
   780→	}
   781→
   782→	// Add parent if not a new branch
   783→	if parentHash != plumbing.ZeroHash {
   784→		commit.ParentHashes = []plumbing.Hash{parentHash}
   785→	}
   786→
   787→	obj := s.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   788→	if err := commit.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   789→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode commit: %w", err)
   790→	}
   791→
   792→	hash, err := s.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   793→	if err != nil {
   794→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store commit: %w", err)
   795→	}
   796→
   797→	return hash, nil
   798→}

   803→// FlattenTree recursively flattens a tree into a map of full paths to entries.
   804→func FlattenTree(repo *git.Repository, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   805→	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
   806→		fullPath := entry.Name
   807→		if prefix != "" {
   808→			fullPath = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
   809→		}
   810→
   811→		if entry.Mode == filemode.Dir {
   812→			// Recurse into subtree
   813→			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
   814→			if err != nil {
   815→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to get subtree %s: %w", fullPath, err)
   816→			}
   817→			if err := FlattenTree(repo, subtree, fullPath, entries); err != nil {
   818→				return err
   819→			}
   820→		} else {
   821→			entries[fullPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   822→				Name: fullPath,
   823→				Mode: entry.Mode,
   824→				Hash: entry.Hash,
   825→			}
   826→		}
   827→	}
   828→	return nil
   829→}

   832→func fileExists(path string) bool {

   837→// createBlobFromFile creates a blob object from a file in the working directory.
   838→func createBlobFromFile(repo *git.Repository, filePath string) (plumbing.Hash, filemode.FileMode, error) {
   839→	info, err := os.Stat(filePath)
   840→	if err != nil {
   841→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to stat file: %w", err)
   842→	}
   843→
   844→	// Determine file mode
   845→	mode := filemode.Regular
   846→	if info.Mode()&0o111 != 0 {
   847→		mode = filemode.Executable
   848→	}
   849→	if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
   850→		mode = filemode.Symlink
   851→	}
   852→
   853→	// Read file contents
   854→	content, err := os.ReadFile(filePath) //nolint:gosec // filePath comes from walking the repository
   855→	if err != nil {
   856→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to read file: %w", err)
   857→	}
   858→
   859→	// Create blob object
   860→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   861→	obj.SetType(plumbing.BlobObject)
   862→	obj.SetSize(int64(len(content)))
   863→
   864→	writer, err := obj.Writer()
   865→	if err != nil {
   866→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to get object writer: %w", err)
   867→	}
   868→
   869→	_, err = writer.Write(content)
   870→	if err != nil {
   871→		_ = writer.Close()
   872→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to write blob content: %w", err)
   873→	}
   874→	if err := writer.Close(); err != nil {
   875→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to close blob writer: %w", err)
   876→	}
   877→
   878→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   879→	if err != nil {
   880→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to store blob object: %w", err)
   881→	}
   882→
   883→	return hash, mode, nil
   884→}

   886→// addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath recursively adds all files in a directory to the entries map.
   887→func addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(repo *git.Repository, dirPathAbs, dirPathRel string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   888→	err := filepath.Walk(dirPathAbs, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
   889→		if err != nil {
   890→			return err
   891→		}
   892→
   893→		// Skip symlinks to prevent reading files outside the metadata directory.
   894→		// A symlink could point to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd) which would
   895→		// then be captured in the checkpoint and stored in git history.
   896→		// NOTE: filepath.Walk uses os.Stat (follows symlinks), so info.Mode() never
   897→		// reports ModeSymlink. We use os.Lstat to check the entry itself.
   898→		// This check MUST come before IsDir() because Walk follows symlinked
   899→		// directories and would recurse into them otherwise.
   900→		linfo, lstatErr := os.Lstat(path)
   901→		if lstatErr != nil {
   902→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to lstat %s: %w", path, lstatErr)
   903→		}
   904→		if linfo.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
   905→			if info.IsDir() {
   906→				return filepath.SkipDir
   907→			}
   908→			return nil
   909→		}
   910→
   911→		if info.IsDir() {
   912→			return nil
   913→		}
   914→
   915→		// Calculate relative path within the directory, then join with dirPathRel for tree entry
   916→		relWithinDir, err := filepath.Rel(dirPathAbs, path)
   917→		if err != nil {
   918→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get relative path for %s: %w", path, err)
   919→		}
   920→
   921→		// Prevent path traversal via symlinks pointing outside the metadata dir
   922→		if strings.HasPrefix(relWithinDir, "..") {
   923→			return fmt.Errorf("path traversal detected: %s", relWithinDir)
   924→		}
   925→
   926→		treePath := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(dirPathRel, relWithinDir))
   927→
   928→		blobHash, mode, err := createRedactedBlobFromFile(repo, path, treePath)
   929→		if err != nil {
   930→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create blob for %s: %w", path, err)
   931→		}
   932→		entries[treePath] = object.TreeEntry{
   933→			Name: treePath,
   934→			Mode: mode,
   935→			Hash: blobHash,
   936→		}
   937→		return nil
   938→	})
   939→	if err != nil {
   940→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to walk directory %s: %w", dirPathAbs, err)
   941→	}
   942→	return nil
   943→}

   945→// treeNode represents a node in our tree structure.
   946→type treeNode struct {
   947→	entries map[string]*treeNode // subdirectories
   948→	files   []object.TreeEntry   // files in this directory
   949→}
   950→
   951→// BuildTreeFromEntries builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries.
   952→// Exported for use by strategy package (push_common.go, session_test.go)
   953→func BuildTreeFromEntries(repo *git.Repository, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   954→	// Build a tree structure
   955→	root := &treeNode{
   956→		entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   957→		files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   958→	}
   959→
   960→	// Insert all entries into the tree structure
   961→	for fullPath, entry := range entries {
   962→		parts := strings.Split(fullPath, "/")
   963→		insertIntoTree(root, parts, entry)
   964→	}
   965→
   966→	// Recursively build tree objects from bottom up
   967→	return buildTreeObject(repo, root)
   968→}
   969→
   970→// insertIntoTree inserts a file entry into the tree structure.
   971→func insertIntoTree(node *treeNode, pathParts []string, entry object.TreeEntry) {
   972→	if len(pathParts) == 1 {
   973→		// This is a file in the current directory
   974→		node.files = append(node.files, object.TreeEntry{
   975→			Name: pathParts[0],
   976→			Mode: entry.Mode,
   977→			Hash: entry.Hash,
   978→		})
   979→		return
   980→	}
   981→
   982→	// This is in a subdirectory
   983→	dirName := pathParts[0]
   984→	if node.entries[dirName] == nil {
   985→		node.entries[dirName] = &treeNode{
   986→			entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   987→			files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   988→		}
   989→	}
   990→	insertIntoTree(node.entries[dirName], pathParts[1:], entry)
   991→}
   992→
   993→// buildTreeObject recursively builds tree objects from a treeNode.
   994→func buildTreeObject(repo *git.Repository, node *treeNode) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   995→	var treeEntries []object.TreeEntry
   996→
   997→	// Add files
   998→	treeEntries = append(treeEntries, node.files...)
   999→
  1000→	// Recursively build subtrees
  1001→	for name, subnode := range node.entries {
  1002→		subHash, err := buildTreeObject(repo, subnode)
  1003→		if err != nil {
  1004→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
  1005→		}
  1006→		treeEntries = append(treeEntries, object.TreeEntry{
  1007→			Name: name,
  1008→			Mode: filemode.Dir,
  1009→			Hash: subHash,
  1010→		})
  1011→	}
  1012→
  1013→	// Sort entries (git requires sorted entries)
  1014→	sortTreeEntries(treeEntries)
  1015→
  1016→	// Create tree object
  1017→	tree := &object.Tree{Entries: treeEntries}
  1018→
  1019→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
  1020→	if err := tree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
  1021→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode tree: %w", err)
  1022→	}
  1023→
  1024→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
  1025→	if err != nil {
  1026→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store tree: %w", err)
  1027→	}
  1028→
  1029→	return hash, nil
  1030→}
  1031→
  1032→// sortTreeEntries sorts tree entries in git's required order.
  1033→// Git sorts tree entries by name, with directories having a trailing /
  1034→func sortTreeEntries(entries []object.TreeEntry) {
  1035→	sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
  1036→		nameI := entries[i].Name
  1037→		nameJ := entries[j].Name
  1038→		if entries[i].Mode == filemode.Dir {
  1039→			nameI += "/"
  1040→		}
  1041→		if entries[j].Mode == filemode.Dir {
  1042→			nameJ += "/"
  1043→		}
  1044→		return nameI < nameJ
  1045→	})
  1046→}
  1047→
  1048→// collectChangedFiles collects all changed files (modified tracked + untracked non-ignored)
  1049→// using git CLI. This is much faster than filesystem walk and respects all gitignore sources
  1050→// including global gitignore (core.excludesfile).
  1051→//
  1052→// Uses git CLI instead of go-git because go-git's worktree.Status() does not respect
  1053→// global gitignore, which can cause globally ignored files to appear as untracked.
  1054→// See: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/129
  1055→//
  1056→// changedFilesResult contains both changed and deleted files from git status.
  1057→type changedFilesResult struct {
  1058→	Changed []string // Files to include (modified, added, untracked, renamed, etc.)
  1059→	Deleted []string // Files that were deleted (need to be excluded from checkpoint tree)
  1060→}
  1061→
  1062→// collectChangedFiles returns all changed files from git status for the first checkpoint.
  1063→//
  1064→// For the first checkpoint, we need to capture:
  1065→// - Modified tracked files (user's uncommitted changes)
  1066→// - Untracked non-ignored files (new files not yet added to git)
  1067→// - Renamed/copied files (both source removal and destination)
  1068→// - Deleted files (to exclude from checkpoint tree)
  1069→//
  1070→// The base tree from HEAD already contains all unchanged tracked files.
  1071→//
  1072→// Uses `git status --porcelain -z` for reliable parsing of filenames with special characters.
  1073→func collectChangedFiles(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) (changedFilesResult, error) {
  1074→	// Get worktree root directory for running git command
  1075→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
  1076→	if err != nil {
  1077→		return changedFilesResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
  1078→	}
  1079→	repoRoot := wt.Filesystem.Root()
  1080→
  1081→	// Use -z for NUL-separated output (handles quoted filenames with spaces/special chars)
  1082→	// Use -uall to list individual untracked files instead of collapsed directories.
  1083→	// Note: CLAUDE.md warns against -uall for user-facing display, but we need the full list
  1084→	// for checkpointing.
  1085→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "-uall")
  1086→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
  1087→	output, err := cmd.Output()
  1088→	if err != nil {
  1089→		return changedFilesResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get git status in %s: %w", repoRoot, err)
  1090→	}
  1091→
  1092→	changedSeen := make(map[string]struct{})
  1093→	deletedSeen := make(map[string]struct{})
  1094→
  1095→	// Parse NUL-separated output
  1096→	// Format: XY filename\0 (for most entries)
  1097→	// For renames/copies: XY newname\0oldname\0
  1098→	entries := strings.Split(string(output), "\x00")
  1099→
  1100→	for i := 0; i < len(entries); i++ {
  1101→		entry := entries[i]
  1102→		if len(entry) < 3 {
  1103→			continue
  1104→		}
  1105→
  1106→		// git status --porcelain format: XY filename
  1107→		// X = staging status, Y = worktree status
  1108→		staging := entry[0]
  1109→		wtStatus := entry[1]
  1110→		filename := entry[3:] // No TrimSpace needed with -z format
  1111→
  1112→		// Handle R/C (rename/copy) first - they have a second entry we must skip
  1113→		// even if the new filename is an infrastructure path
  1114→		if staging == 'R' || staging == 'C' {
  1115→			// Renamed or copied: current entry is new name, next entry is old name
  1116→			if !paths.IsInfrastructurePath(filename) {
  1117→				changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1118→			}
  1119→			// The old name follows as the next NUL-separated entry - must always skip it
  1120→			if i+1 < len(entries) && entries[i+1] != "" {
  1121→				oldName := entries[i+1]
  1122→				if staging == 'R' && !paths.IsInfrastructurePath(oldName) {
  1123→					// For renames, old file is effectively deleted
  1124→					deletedSeen[oldName] = struct{}{}
  1125→				}
  1126→				i++ // Skip the old name entry
  1127→			}
  1128→			continue
  1129→		}
  1130→
  1131→		// Skip .entire directory for non-R/C entries
  1132→		if paths.IsInfrastructurePath(filename) {
  1133→			continue
  1134→		}
  1135→
  1136→		// Handle different status codes
  1137→		switch {
  1138→		case staging == 'D' || wtStatus == 'D':
  1139→			// Deleted file - track separately
  1140→			deletedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1141→
  1142→		case wtStatus == 'M' || wtStatus == 'A':
  1143→			// Modified or added in worktree
  1144→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1145→
  1146→		case staging == '?' && wtStatus == '?':
  1147→			// Untracked file
  1148→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1149→
  1150→		case staging == 'A' || staging == 'M':
  1151→			// Staged add or modify
  1152→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1153→
  1154→		case staging == 'T' || wtStatus == 'T':
  1155→			// Type change (e.g., file to symlink)
  1156→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1157→
  1158→		case staging == 'U' || wtStatus == 'U':
  1159→			// Unmerged (conflict) - include current file state
  1160→			changedSeen[filename] = struct{}{}
  1161→		}
  1162→	}
  1163→
  1164→	changed := make([]string, 0, len(changedSeen))
  1165→	for file := range changedSeen {
  1166→		changed = append(changed, file)
  1167→	}
  1168→
  1169→	deleted := make([]string, 0, len(deletedSeen))
  1170→	for file := range deletedSeen {
  1171→		deleted = append(deleted, file)
  1172→	}
  1173→
  1174→	return changedFilesResult{Changed: changed, Deleted: deleted}, nil
  1175→}

	dir := t.TempDir()

	if err != nil {

	headData, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "HEAD"))

package cli

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/trailers"

	"github.com/charmbracelet/huh"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/object"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

func newResumeCmd() *cobra.Command {
	var force bool

	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "resume <branch>",
		Short: "Switch to a branch and resume its session",
		Long: `Switch to a local branch and resume the agent session from its last commit.

This command:
1. Checks out the specified branch
2. Finds the session ID from commits unique to this branch (not on main)
3. Restores the session log if it doesn't exist locally
4. Shows the command to resume the session

If the branch doesn't exist locally but exists on origin, you'll be prompted
to fetch it.

If newer commits without checkpoints exist on the branch (e.g., after merging main
or cherry-picking from elsewhere), this operation will reset your Git status to the
most recent commit with a checkpoint.  You'll be prompted to confirm resuming in this case.`,
		Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			if checkDisabledGuard(cmd.OutOrStdout()) {
				return nil
			}
			ctx := cmd.Context()
			return runResume(ctx, args[0], force)
		},
	}

	cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "Resume from older checkpoint without confirmation")

	return cmd
}

The `main` branch (MERGE_HEAD = 7fd8dffc) made various structural changes. The resolution strategy is: take main's structural changes but keep HEAD's `ctx context.Context` parameter additions.

Files to resolve:
1. cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go
2. cmd/entire/cli/logging/logger.go
3. cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/temporary.go
4. cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/hooks_test.go

For each file:
1. Read the file to see the conflict markers
2. Use `git show MERGE_HEAD:<filepath>` via Bash to see main's version
3. Use `git show HEAD:<filepath>` via Bash to see the branch's version
4. The branch's changes: adding `ctx context.Context` to function signatures and passing `ctx` to callees
5. Main's changes: renamed `RepoRoot` to `WorktreeRoot`, various structural improvements

General rules:
- If the branch adds `ctx context.Context` to a function signature, KEEP it
- If main renamed `RepoRoot` to `WorktreeRoot`, use `WorktreeRoot` but WITH the `ctx` parameter: `WorktreeRoot(ctx)`
- Where main added `ctx := context.Background()` or `ctx := context.TODO()`, remove that line since we already have ctx from the parameter
- For paths.go specifically: the function should be named `WorktreeRoot` (main's name) but accept `ctx context.Context` (branch's addition). Remove the `ctx := context.Background()` line that main added since ctx comes from the parameter.
- For AbsPath in paths.go: use `AbsPath(ctx context.Context, relPath string)` and call `WorktreeRoot(ctx)` inside

After resolving conflicts in each file, run `git add <filepath>` on it.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT run tests or lint. Just resolve the conflicts and stage the files. Read each file carefully before editing.

// checkCanRewind checks if working directory is clean enough for rewind.
// Returns (canRewind, reason, error). Shared by shadow and linear-shadow strategies.
func checkCanRewind(ctx context.Context) (bool, string, error) {
	repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
	}

	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
	if err != nil {
		return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
	}

	status, err := worktree.Status()
	if err != nil {
		return false, "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get status: %w", err)
	}

	if status.IsClean() {
		return true, "", nil
	}

	var modified, added, deleted []string
	for file, st := range status {
		// Skip .entire directory
		if paths.IsInfrastructurePath(file) {
			continue
		}

		// Skip untracked files
		if st.Worktree == git.Untracked {
			continue
		}

		switch {
		case st.Staging == git.Added || st.Worktree == git.Added:
			added = append(added, file)
		case st.Staging == git.Deleted || st.Worktree == git.Deleted:
			deleted = append(deleted, file)
		case st.Staging == git.Modified || st.Worktree == git.Modified:
			modified = append(modified, file)
		}
	}

	if len(modified) == 0 && len(added) == 0 && len(deleted) == 0 {
		return true, "", nil
	}

	var msg strings.Builder
	msg.WriteString("You have uncommitted changes:\n")
	for _, f := range modified {
		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  modified:   %s\n", f))
	}
	for _, f := range added {
		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  added:      %s\n", f))
	}
	for _, f := range deleted {
		msg.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  deleted:    %s\n", f))
	}
	msg.WriteString("\nPlease commit or stash your changes before rewinding.")

	return false, msg.String(), nil
}

1→// hook_registry.go provides hook command registration for agents.
     2→// The lifecycle dispatcher (DispatchLifecycleEvent) handles all lifecycle events.
     3→// PostTodo is the only hook that's handled directly (not via lifecycle dispatcher).
     4→package cli
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"context"
     8→	"errors"
     9→	"fmt"
    10→	"log/slog"
    11→	"time"
    12→
    13→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
    14→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode"
    15→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/geminicli"
    16→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    17→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    18→
    19→	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
    20→)
    21→
    22→// agentHookLogCleanup stores the cleanup function for agent hook logging.
    23→// Set by PersistentPreRunE, called by PersistentPostRunE.
    24→var agentHookLogCleanup func()
    25→
    26→// currentHookAgentName stores the agent name for the currently executing hook.
    27→// Set by newAgentHookVerbCmdWithLogging before calling the handler.
    28→// This allows handlers to know which agent invoked the hook without guessing.
    29→var currentHookAgentName agent.AgentName
    30→
    31→// GetCurrentHookAgent returns the agent for the currently executing hook.
    32→// Returns the agent based on the hook command structure (e.g., "entire hooks claude-code ...")
    33→// rather than guessing from directory presence.
    34→// Falls back to GetAgent() if not in a hook context.
    35→func GetCurrentHookAgent() (agent.Agent, error) {
    36→	if currentHookAgentName == "" {
    37→		return nil, errors.New("not in a hook context: agent name not set")
    38→	}
    39→
    40→	ag, err := agent.Get(currentHookAgentName)
    41→	if err != nil {
    42→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("getting hook agent %q: %w", currentHookAgentName, err)
    43→	}
    44→	return ag, nil
    45→}
    46→
    47→// newAgentHooksCmd creates a hooks subcommand for an agent that implements HookSupport.
    48→// It dynamically creates subcommands for each hook the agent supports.
    49→func newAgentHooksCmd(agentName agent.AgentName, handler agent.HookSupport) *cobra.Command {
    50→	cmd := &cobra.Command{
    51→		Use:    string(agentName),
    52→		Short:  handler.Description() + " hook handlers",
    53→		Hidden: true,
    54→		PersistentPreRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
    55→			agentHookLogCleanup = initHookLogging()
    56→			return nil
    57→		},
    58→		PersistentPostRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
    59→			if agentHookLogCleanup != nil {
    60→				agentHookLogCleanup()
    61→			}
    62→			return nil
    63→		},
    64→	}
    65→
    66→	for _, hookName := range handler.HookNames() {

   106→			}

   108→			start := time.Now()
   109→
   110→			// Initialize logging context with agent name
   111→			ctx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "hooks"), agentName)
   112→
   113→			// Get strategy name for logging
   114→			strategyName := GetStrategy().Name()
   115→
   116→			hookType := getHookType(hookName)
   117→
   118→			logging.Debug(ctx, "hook invoked",

   121→				slog.String("strategy", strategyName),

   144→			}

   146→			if event != nil {

   154→

   156→				slog.String("hook", hookName),
   157→				slog.String("hook_type", hookType),
   158→				slog.String("strategy", strategyName),
   159→				slog.Bool("success", hookErr == nil),

1→package cli
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"context"
     5→	"log/slog"
     6→	"time"
     7→
     8→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
     9→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
    10→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    11→
    12→	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
    13→)
    14→
    15→const unknownStrategyName = "unknown"
    16→
    17→// gitHooksDisabled is set by PersistentPreRunE when Entire is not set up or disabled.
    18→// When true, all git hook commands return early without doing any work.
    19→var gitHooksDisabled bool
    20→
    21→// gitHookContext holds common state for git hook logging.
    22→type gitHookContext struct {
    23→	hookName     string
    24→	ctx          context.Context
    25→	start        time.Time
    26→	strategy     strategy.Strategy
    27→	strategyName string
    28→}
    29→
    30→// newGitHookContext creates a new git hook context with logging initialized.
    31→func newGitHookContext(hookName string) *gitHookContext {
    32→	g := &gitHookContext{
    33→		hookName:     hookName,
    34→		start:        time.Now(),
    35→		ctx:          logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "hooks"),
    36→		strategyName: unknownStrategyName,
    37→	}
    38→	g.strategy = GetStrategy()
    39→	g.strategyName = g.strategy.Name()
    40→	return g
    41→}
    42→
    43→// logInvoked logs that the hook was invoked.
    44→func (g *gitHookContext) logInvoked(extraAttrs ...any) {
    45→	attrs := []any{
    46→		slog.String("hook", g.hookName),
    47→		slog.String("hook_type", "git"),
    48→		slog.String("strategy", g.strategyName),
    49→	}
    50→	logging.Debug(g.ctx, g.hookName+" hook invoked", append(attrs, extraAttrs...)...)
    51→}
    52→
    53→// logCompleted logs hook completion with duration at DEBUG level.
    54→// The actual work logging (checkpoint operations) happens at INFO level in the handlers.
    55→func (g *gitHookContext) logCompleted(err error, extraAttrs ...any) {
    56→	attrs := []any{
    57→		slog.String("hook", g.hookName),
    58→		slog.String("hook_type", "git"),
    59→		slog.String("strategy", g.strategyName),
    60→		slog.Bool("success", err == nil),
    61→	}
    62→	logging.LogDuration(g.ctx, slog.LevelDebug, g.hookName+" hook completed", g.start, append(attrs, extraAttrs...)...)
    63→}
    64→
    65→// initHookLogging initializes logging for hooks by finding the most recent session.
    66→// Returns a cleanup function that should be deferred.
    67→// If Entire is not set up or disabled, returns a no-op to avoid creating files.
    68→func initHookLogging() func() {
    69→	// Don't create any files if Entire is not set up or disabled.
    70→	// This is checked here as defense-in-depth (also checked in PersistentPreRunE).
    71→	if !settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled() {
    72→		return func() {}
    73→	}
    74→
    75→	// Set up log level getter so logging can read from settings
    76→	logging.SetLogLevelGetter(GetLogLevel)
    77→
    78→	// Read session ID for the slog attribute (empty string is fine - log file is fixed)
    79→	sessionID := strategy.FindMostRecentSession()
    80→	if err := logging.Init(sessionID); err != nil {
    81→		// Init failed - logging will use stderr fallback
    82→		return func() {}
    83→	}
    84→	return logging.Close
    85→}
    86→
    87→// hookLogCleanup stores the cleanup function for hook logging.
    88→// Set by PersistentPreRunE, called by PersistentPostRunE.
    89→var hookLogCleanup func()
    90→
    91→func newHooksGitCmd() *cobra.Command {
    92→	cmd := &cobra.Command{
    93→		Use:    "git",
    94→		Short:  "Git hook handlers",
    95→		Long:   "Commands called by git hooks. These delegate to the current strategy.",
    96→		Hidden: true, // Internal command, not for direct user use
    97→		PersistentPreRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
    98→			// Check if Entire is set up and enabled before doing any work.
    99→			// This prevents global git hooks from doing anything in repos where
   100→			// Entire was never enabled or has been disabled.
   101→			if !settings.IsSetUpAndEnabled() {
   102→				gitHooksDisabled = true
   103→				return nil
   104→			}
   105→			hookLogCleanup = initHookLogging()
   106→			return nil
   107→		},
   108→		PersistentPostRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
   109→			if hookLogCleanup != nil {
   110→				hookLogCleanup()
   111→			}
   112→			return nil
   113→		},
   114→	}
   115→
   116→	cmd.AddCommand(newHooksGitPrepareCommitMsgCmd())
   117→	cmd.AddCommand(newHooksGitCommitMsgCmd())
   118→	cmd.AddCommand(newHooksGitPostCommitCmd())
   119→	cmd.AddCommand(newHooksGitPrePushCmd())
   120→
   121→	return cmd
   122→}
   123→
   124→func newHooksGitPrepareCommitMsgCmd() *cobra.Command {
   125→	return &cobra.Command{
   126→		Use:   "prepare-commit-msg <commit-msg-file> [source]",
   127→		Short: "Handle prepare-commit-msg git hook",
   128→		Args:  cobra.RangeArgs(1, 2),
   129→		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
   130→			if gitHooksDisabled {
   131→				return nil
   132→			}
   133→
   134→			commitMsgFile := args[0]
   135→			var source string
   136→			if len(args) > 1 {
   137→				source = args[1]
   138→			}
   139→
   140→			g := newGitHookContext("prepare-commit-msg")
   141→			g.logInvoked(slog.String("source", source))
   142→
   143→			hookErr := g.strategy.PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile, source)
   144→			g.logCompleted(hookErr, slog.String("source", source))
   145→
   146→			return nil
   147→		},
   148→	}
   149→}
   150→
   151→func newHooksGitCommitMsgCmd() *cobra.Command {
   152→	return &cobra.Command{
   153→		Use:   "commit-msg <commit-msg-file>",
   154→		Short: "Handle commit-msg git hook",
   155→		Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   156→		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
   157→			if gitHooksDisabled {
   158→				return nil
   159→			}
   160→
   161→			commitMsgFile := args[0]
   162→
   163→			g := newGitHookContext("commit-msg")
   164→			g.logInvoked()
   165→
   166→			hookErr := g.strategy.CommitMsg(commitMsgFile)
   167→			g.logCompleted(hookErr)
   168→			return hookErr //nolint:wrapcheck // Thin delegation layer - wrapping adds no value
   169→		},
   170→	}
   171→}
   172→
   173→func newHooksGitPostCommitCmd() *cobra.Command {
   174→	return &cobra.Command{
   175→		Use:   "post-commit",
   176→		Short: "Handle post-commit git hook",
   177→		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
   178→		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
   179→			if gitHooksDisabled {
   180→				return nil
   181→			}
   182→
   183→			g := newGitHookContext("post-commit")
   184→			g.logInvoked()
   185→
   186→			hookErr := g.strategy.PostCommit()
   187→			g.logCompleted(hookErr)
   188→
   189→			return nil
   190→		},
   191→	}
   192→}
   193→
   194→func newHooksGitPrePushCmd() *cobra.Command {
   195→	return &cobra.Command{
   196→		Use:   "pre-push <remote>",
   197→		Short: "Handle pre-push git hook",
   198→		Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   199→		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
   200→			if gitHooksDisabled {
   201→				return nil
   202→			}
   203→
   204→			remote := args[0]
   205→
   206→			g := newGitHookContext("pre-push")
   207→			g.logInvoked(slog.String("remote", remote))
   208→
   209→			hookErr := g.strategy.PrePush(remote)
   210→			g.logCompleted(hookErr, slog.String("remote", remote))
   211→
   212→			return nil
   213→		},
   214→	}
   215→}

1→// lifecycle.go implements the generic lifecycle event dispatcher.
     2→// It routes normalized events from any agent to the appropriate framework actions.
     3→//
     4→// The dispatcher inverts the current flow from "agent handler calls framework functions"
     5→// to "framework dispatcher calls agent methods." Agents are passive data providers;
     6→// the dispatcher handles all orchestration: state transitions, strategy calls,
     7→// file change detection, metadata generation.
     8→package cli
     9→
    10→import (
    11→	"context"
    12→	"errors"
    13→	"fmt"
    14→	"log/slog"
    15→	"os"
    16→	"path/filepath"
    17→	"strings"
    18→	"time"
    19→
    20→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
    21→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    22→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    23→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
    24→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    25→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/transcript"
    26→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/validation"
    27→)
    28→
    29→// DispatchLifecycleEvent routes a normalized lifecycle event to the appropriate handler.
    30→// Returns nil if the event was handled successfully.
    31→func DispatchLifecycleEvent(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
    32→	if ag == nil {
    33→		return errors.New("agent cannot be nil")
    34→	}
    35→	if event == nil {
    36→		return errors.New("event cannot be nil")
    37→	}
    38→
    39→	switch event.Type {
    40→	case agent.SessionStart:
    41→		return handleLifecycleSessionStart(ag, event)
    42→	case agent.TurnStart:
    43→		return handleLifecycleTurnStart(ag, event)
    44→	case agent.TurnEnd:
    45→		return handleLifecycleTurnEnd(ag, event)
    46→	case agent.Compaction:
    47→		return handleLifecycleCompaction(ag, event)
    48→	case agent.SessionEnd:
    49→		return handleLifecycleSessionEnd(ag, event)
    50→	case agent.SubagentStart:
    51→		return handleLifecycleSubagentStart(ag, event)
    52→	case agent.SubagentEnd:
    53→		return handleLifecycleSubagentEnd(ag, event)
    54→	default:
    55→		return fmt.Errorf("unknown lifecycle event type: %d", event.Type)
    56→	}
    57→}
    58→
    59→// handleLifecycleSessionStart handles session start: shows banner, checks concurrent sessions,
    60→// fires state machine transition.
    61→func handleLifecycleSessionStart(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
    62→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
    63→	logging.Info(logCtx, "session-start",
    64→		slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
    65→		slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
    66→		slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
    67→	)
    68→
    69→	if event.SessionID == "" {
    70→		return fmt.Errorf("no session_id in %s event", event.Type)
    71→	}
    72→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(event.SessionID); err != nil {
    73→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
    74→	}
    75→
    76→	// Build informational message
    77→	message := "\n\nPowered by Entire:\n  This conversation will be linked to your next commit."
    78→
    79→	// Check for concurrent sessions and append count if any
    80→	strat := GetStrategy()
    81→	if count, err := strat.CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(event.SessionID); err == nil && count > 0 {
    82→		message += fmt.Sprintf("\n  %d other active conversation(s) in this workspace will also be included.\n  Use 'entire status' for more information.", count)
    83→	}
    84→
    85→	// Output informational message
    86→	if event.ResponseMessage != "" {
    87→		message = event.ResponseMessage
    88→	}
    89→	if err := outputHookResponse(message); err != nil {
    90→		return err

   383→func runRewindToInternal(commitID string, logsOnly bool, reset bool) error {
   384→	start := GetStrategy()
   385→
   386→	// Check for uncommitted changes (skip for reset which handles this itself)
   387→	if !reset {
   388→		canRewind, changeMsg, err := start.CanRewind()
   389→		if err != nil {
   390→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check for uncommitted changes: %w", err)
   391→		}
   392→		if !canRewind {
   393→			return fmt.Errorf("%s", changeMsg)
   394→		}
   395→	}
   396→
   397→	// Get rewind points
   398→	points, err := start.GetRewindPoints(20)
   399→	if err != nil {
   400→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to find rewind points: %w", err)
   401→	}
   402→
   403→	// Find the matching point (support both full and short commit IDs)
   404→	var selectedPoint *strategy.RewindPoint
   405→	for _, p := range points {
   406→		if p.ID == commitID || (len(commitID) >= 7 && len(p.ID) >= 7 && strings.HasPrefix(p.ID, commitID)) {
   407→			pointCopy := p
   408→			selectedPoint = &pointCopy
   409→			break
   410→		}
   411→	}
   412→
   413→	if selectedPoint == nil {
   414→		return fmt.Errorf("rewind point not found: %s", commitID)
   415→	}
   416→
   417→	// Handle reset mode (for logs-only points)
   418→	if reset {
   419→		return handleLogsOnlyResetNonInteractive(start, *selectedPoint)
   420→	}
   421→
   422→	// Handle logs-only restoration:
   423→	// 1. For logs-only points, always use logs-only restoration
   424→	// 2. If --logs-only flag is set, use logs-only restoration even for checkpoint points
   425→	if selectedPoint.IsLogsOnly || logsOnly {
   426→		return handleLogsOnlyRewindNonInteractive(start, *selectedPoint)
   427→	}
   428→
   429→	// Preview rewind to show warnings about files that will be deleted
   430→	preview, previewErr := start.PreviewRewind(*selectedPoint)
   431→	if previewErr == nil && preview != nil && len(preview.FilesToDelete) > 0 {
   432→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nWarning: The following untracked files will be DELETED:\n")
   433→		for _, f := range preview.FilesToDelete {
   434→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  - %s\n", f)
   435→		}
   436→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\n")
   437→	}
   438→
   439→	// Resolve agent once for use throughout
   440→	agent, err := getAgent(selectedPoint.Agent)
   441→	if err != nil {
   442→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get agent: %w", err)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	// Initialize logging context with agent from checkpoint
   446→	ctx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "rewind")
   447→	ctx = logging.WithAgent(ctx, agent.Name())
   448→
   449→	logging.Debug(ctx, "rewind started",
   450→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   451→		slog.String("session_id", selectedPoint.SessionID),
   452→		slog.Bool("is_task_checkpoint", selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint),
   453→	)
   454→
   455→	// Perform the rewind
   456→	if err := start.Rewind(*selectedPoint); err != nil {
   457→		logging.Error(ctx, "rewind failed",
   458→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   459→			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   460→		)
   461→		return err //nolint:wrapcheck // already present in codebase
   462→	}
   463→
   464→	logging.Debug(ctx, "rewind completed",
   465→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", selectedPoint.ID),
   466→	)
   467→
   468→	// Handle transcript restoration
   469→	var sessionID string
   470→	var transcriptFile string
   471→
   472→	if selectedPoint.IsTaskCheckpoint {
   473→		checkpoint, err := start.GetTaskCheckpoint(*selectedPoint)
   474→		if err != nil {
   475→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to read task checkpoint: %v\n", err)
   476→			return nil
   477→		}
   478→
   479→		sessionID = checkpoint.SessionID
   480→
   481→		if checkpoint.CheckpointUUID != "" {
   482→			// Use strategy-based transcript restoration for task checkpoints
   483→			if err := restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript(start, *selectedPoint, sessionID, checkpoint.CheckpointUUID, agent); err != nil {
   484→				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore truncated session transcript: %v\n", err)
   485→			} else {
   486→				fmt.Printf("Rewound to task checkpoint. %s\n", agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   487→			}
   488→			return nil
   489→		}
   490→	} else {
   491→		// Prefer SessionID from trailer over path-based extraction
   492→		sessionID = selectedPoint.SessionID
   493→		if sessionID == "" {
   494→			sessionID = filepath.Base(selectedPoint.MetadataDir)
   495→		}
   496→		transcriptFile = filepath.Join(selectedPoint.MetadataDir, paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy)
   497→	}
   498→
   499→	// Try to restore transcript using the appropriate method:
   500→	// 1. Checkpoint storage (committed checkpoints with valid checkpoint ID)
   501→	// 2. Shadow branch (uncommitted checkpoints with commit hash)
   502→	// 3. Local file (active sessions)
   503→	var restored bool
   504→	if !selectedPoint.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   505→		// Try checkpoint storage first for committed checkpoints
   506→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromStrategy(selectedPoint.CheckpointID, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   507→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   508→			restored = true
   509→		}
   510→	}
   511→
   512→	if !restored && selectedPoint.MetadataDir != "" && len(selectedPoint.ID) == 40 {
   513→		// Try shadow branch for uncommitted checkpoints (ID is a 40-char commit hash)
   514→		if returnedSessionID, err := restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow(selectedPoint.ID, selectedPoint.MetadataDir, sessionID, agent); err == nil {
   515→			sessionID = returnedSessionID
   516→			restored = true
   517→		}
   518→	}
   519→
   520→	if !restored {
   521→		// Fall back to local file
   522→		if err := restoreSessionTranscript(transcriptFile, sessionID, agent); err != nil {
   523→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to restore session transcript: %v\n", err)
   524→		}
   525→	}
   526→
   527→	fmt.Printf("Rewound to %s. %s\n", selectedPoint.ID[:7], agent.FormatResumeCommand(sessionID))
   528→	return nil
   529→}

   692→// restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow restores a session transcript from a shadow branch commit.

   694→func restoreSessionTranscriptFromShadow(commitHash, metadataDir, sessionID string, agent agentpkg.Agent) (string, error) {
   695→	// Open repository
   696→	repo, err := git.PlainOpenWithOptions(".", &git.PlainOpenOptions{DetectDotGit: true})
   697→	if err != nil {
   698→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
   699→	}

   701→	// Parse commit hash
   702→	hash := plumbing.NewHash(commitHash)
   703→	if hash.IsZero() {
   704→		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid commit hash: %s", commitHash)
   705→	}
   706→
   707→	// Get transcript from shadow branch commit tree
   708→	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)
   709→	content, err := store.GetTranscriptFromCommit(hash, metadataDir, agent.Type())
   710→	if err != nil {
   711→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get transcript from shadow branch: %w", err)
   712→	}
   713→
   714→	sessionFile, err := resolveTranscriptPath(sessionID, agent)
   715→	if err != nil {

   717→	}

   719→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create agent session directory: %w", err)
   720→	}
   721→	agentSession := &agentpkg.AgentSession{
   722→		SessionID:  sessionID,
   723→		AgentName:  agent.Name(),
   724→		SessionRef: sessionFile,
   725→		NativeData: content,
   726→	}
   727→	if err := agent.WriteSession(agentSession); err != nil {
   728→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to write session: %w", err)
   729→	}
   730→	return sessionID, nil
   731→}

   733→// restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript restores a truncated transcript for a task checkpoint.

   737→// TruncateTranscriptAtUUID, writeTranscript) assumes Claude's JSONL format.
   738→// This is acceptable because task checkpoints are currently only created by Claude Code's
   739→// PostToolUse hook. If other agents gain sub-agent support, this will need a
   740→// format-aware refactor (agent-specific parsing, truncation, and serialization).
   741→func restoreTaskCheckpointTranscript(strat strategy.Strategy, point strategy.RewindPoint, sessionID, checkpointUUID string, agent agentpkg.Agent) error {

   750→	if err != nil {

   752→	}
   753→

   755→	truncated := TruncateTranscriptAtUUID(parsed, checkpointUUID)
   756→
   757→	sessionFile, err := resolveTranscriptPath(sessionID, agent)
   758→	if err != nil {

   769→	if err := writeTranscript(sessionFile, truncated); err != nil {

  1021→// getCurrentHeadHash returns the current HEAD commit hash.
  1022→func getCurrentHeadHash() (string, error) {
  1023→	repo, err := openRepository()

  1036→// checkResetSafety checks for potential issues before a git reset --hard.
  1037→// Returns a list of warning messages (empty if safe to proceed without warnings).
  1038→// If uncommittedChangesWarning is provided, it will be used instead of a generic warning.
  1039→func checkResetSafety(targetCommitHash string, uncommittedChangesWarning string) ([]string, error) {
  1040→	var warnings []string
  1041→
  1042→	repo, err := openRepository()
  1043→	if err != nil {
  1044→		return nil, err
  1045→	}
  1046→

  1055→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
  1056→		}

  1061→		}

  1065→		}
  1066→	}

  1090→// countCommitsBetween counts commits between ancestor and descendant.
  1091→// Returns 0 if ancestor == descendant, -1 on error.
  1092→func countCommitsBetween(repo *git.Repository, ancestor, descendant plumbing.Hash) (int, error) {
  1093→	if ancestor == descendant {
  1094→		return 0, nil
  1095→	}
  1096→
  1097→	// Walk from descendant back to ancestor
  1098→	count := 0
  1099→	current := descendant
  1100→
  1101→	for count < 1000 { // Safety limit
  1102→		if current == ancestor {
  1103→			return count, nil
  1104→		}
  1105→
  1106→		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(current)
  1107→		if err != nil {
  1108→			return -1, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
  1109→		}
  1110→
  1111→		if commit.NumParents() == 0 {
  1112→			// Reached root without finding ancestor - ancestor not in history
  1113→			return -1, nil
  1114→		}
  1115→
  1116→		count++
  1117→		current = commit.ParentHashes[0] // Follow first parent
  1118→	}
  1119→
  1120→	return -1, nil
  1121→}

  1125→// deletes untracked directories (like .entire/) even when they're in .gitignore.
  1126→func performGitResetHard(commitHash string) error {

  1141→func sanitizeForTerminal(s string) string {
  1142→	var result strings.Builder
  1143→	result.Grow(len(s))
  1144→
  1145→	for _, r := range s {
  1146→		// Skip emoji skin tone modifiers (U+1F3FB to U+1F3FF)
  1147→		if r >= 0x1F3FB && r <= 0x1F3FF {
  1148→			continue

  1157→		}

  1161→		}
  1162→	}
